newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Benpres sees 1996 net about 2.0 bln pesos.
newsitem.headline: Benpres sees 1996 net about 2.0 bln pesos.

text.p: Benpres Holdings Corp Chief Operating Officer J. Xavier Gonzales told Reuters on Wednesday the company was expected to post a net profit of around 2.0 billion pesos in 1996, up 25 percent from the year-ago figure.
Net profits in 1997 were seen at about 2.5 billion pesos, he said.
"We will easily see a 25 percent total earnings growth in 1996 or about 2.0 billion pesos," Gonzales said in an interview.
"(For 1997) there's a good chance of doing a little over 25 percent or about 2.5 billion pesos," he added.

ABS-CBN Broadcasting Corp, which accounts for 50 to 55 percent of Benpres' earnings, was expected to sustain a 20 percent growth in earnings in 1996 assuming a 12 to 14 percent growth in advertising growth, he said.
Gonzales said his firm's income will be enhanced by the contribution of real estate unit Rockwell Land Corp in 1997.
"Our telecoms subsidiary will start contributing in 1998 and our tollway subsidiary in 1999," he said.
Gonzales said the Benpres group will spend 27.5 billion pesos this year on expansion.

Bayan Telecommunications is expected to eat up the biggest chunk with a programmed expenditute of 10 billion pesos. The firm plans to rehabilitate its newly acquired cellular phone unit Express Telecommunications Co, and to expand its fixed-telephone system, Gonzales said.

ABS-CBN is spending another two billion pesos for the construction of its building and provincial expansion while Sky Cable, the country's largest cable TV provider, will spend 1.5 billion pesos on expansion.

First Philippine Holdings Corp will spend three billion pesos, First Gas Holdings Corp will shell two billion pesos, Rockwell Land will spend four billion pesos, while tollway operator Philippine Infrastructure Development Corp is expected to spend five billion pesos.
